extracted.intended_audience: colleges and universities, Title IX coordinators, students, faculty, administrators, policymakers, advocates, and attorneys engaged with Title IX rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and evaluative criteria related to Department of Education Title IX rulemaking and campus grievance procedures, based on public comments and the Department's discussion of changes. Focuses on procedural protections, scope, definitions, and implementation practices for higher education institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures regardless of participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations ensure that recipients offer supportive measures to complainants regardless of participation in a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department changed rules so supportive measures are offered to complainants even if they do not participate in formal proceedings; cited as a change in response to commenters who recounted benefits of Title IX supportive services.

rubrics_metrics.name: No punishment until completion of grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents cannot be punished until the completion of a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations ensure respondents are not disciplined before the grievance process concludes — cited as a safeguard for due process and a change responding to commenters' concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment rulemaking rather than guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use formal notice-and-comment rulemaking procedures (APA) instead of sub-regulatory guidance to implement Title IX reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters praised rulemaking as critical for gathering informed feedback, strengthening rule of law, providing legal clarity and certainty, creating mandatory standards (safe harbors), and reducing litigation and confusion that arose from guidance (e.g., Dear Colleague letters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Codified standards for clarity, consistency, and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Codified rules provide a transparent standard institutions must meet and make it easier for colleges and universities to comply with Title IX, align obligations, and enable public accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued that formal regulations reduce subjective agency discretion, create certainty by replacing nebulous guidance, and help align Title IX with other obligations (e.g., Clery Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear investigation procedures and written notice to both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations must proceed with clear directives and written notice must be provided to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters supported clear directives about how investigations must proceed and complained where there was lack of notice of charges, lack of details about offenses, or evidence being withheld until after the response opportunity. Final regulations discuss written notice and procedural clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to investigative materials and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have access to investigation documents/evidence and a meaningful opportunity to respond before determinations are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous commenters described investigation reports or evidence being shown to respondents only after their opportunity to respond had passed; the rule discussion emphasizes transparency and opportunity to challenge evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards and institutional flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions have the opportunity to use a higher evidentiary standard when adjudicating Title IX matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted support for allowing schools to choose evidentiary standards (for example, beyond a preponderance of the evidence); the final regulations permit some flexibility while setting minimum procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sexual harassment: clarity and appropriate scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of sexual harassment must be clear in scope — sufficiently covering conduct that impairs educational access while avoiding over-breadth that yields nonsensical outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters feared the proposed definition might exclude certain rapes or be too narrow; others feared a broad definition produced absurd investigations. The Department discusses balancing coverage of sex discrimination with clear boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process protections and presumption of innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must respect respondents' due process rights, including protections against being presumed guilty and fair opportunity to present their side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many commenters recounted expulsions, firings, suspensions, or disciplinary actions without adequate opportunity to be heard. The Department cites non-negotiable principles including the right of accused persons to know that guilt is not predetermined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be informed of charges and detailed allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents must be notified of the charges, the details of alleged offenses, and evidence used against them in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters described lack of notice of charges or the details and evidence; final regulations emphasize written notice and procedural transparency so parties can respond effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to representation and advisors during proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties should be able to have representation or an advisor present during Title IX interviews or hearings, and advisors should be able to meaningfully participate consistent with institutional procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters reported being denied representation or that their lawyers/advisors were not allowed to speak; the Department discusses rules about advisors and procedural role to ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination and mechanisms to test credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for challenging witness credibility — including the question of whether and how cross-examination occurs — must balance trauma concerns with the need to test evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters said cross-examination is traumatic and would deter reporting; others described harm from not being able to cross-examine, hearsay being admitted without challenge, and being unable to test credibility. The public comments reflect this tension and inform how the Department frames hearing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial decision-makers and conflict-free appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals from determinations regarding responsibility must be decided by decision-makers who are free from conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 106.45(b)(8) requires appeal decision-makers be free of conflicts; commenters emphasized the importance of impartiality and independence in adjudication and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely resolution of cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance processes should resolve matters within a reasonable timeframe to avoid prolonged harm; delays of six to twelve months impose severe consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters reported lengthy processes (six to 12 months or more) and harms including suspension from school during this time; regulations set timelines for prompt resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protections and limiting public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures should protect complainant and respondent confidentiality where appropriate to avoid public embarrassment, retaliation, or chilling of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recounted names not being kept confidential, public embarrassment causing students to quit teams or drop out, and fears that public nature of proceedings deters reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear scope of Title IX coverage (where and to whom it applies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must clarify the education programs or activities covered by Title IX (e.g., including recognized student organizations, buildings owned/controlled by student organizations, fraternities/sororities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters debated whether fraternities, sororities, or certain programs are covered; final regs specify inclusion (e.g., §106.44(a) includes buildings owned or controlled by recognized student organizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability accommodations within the process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide appropriate accommodations for parties with disabilities (e.g., autism) during investigations and hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted denials of autism accommodations or other disability supports; the Department recognizes need to honor accommodation requests throughout the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards against retaliatory or opportunistic charging
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures should prevent institutions from inventing new charges or using the process retaliatorily once original charges falter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several commenters feared institutional retaliation, such as new charges being invented after original allegations fell apart; rules and oversight should reduce such practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating severe financial burdens on respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the financial costs to respondents and families (legal and medical fees) and the disparate impact on lower- and moderate-income students should inform policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters described legal costs ranging from $10,000 to over $100,000 and urged study of the effects of prior policies on financially disadvantaged students; the Department noted these concerns in discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention, education, and supportive services as complements to adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and institutional responses should include prevention measures (consent education, bystander training), counseling, restorative justice, and community-based supports in addition to grievance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended alternatives and complements to adjudication such as behavioral therapy for offenders, bystander intervention training, best practices for supporting survivors, restorative justice, and independent investigatory bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retroactivity of final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations will not be enforced retroactively; they will not require reopening of past disciplinary cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters requested retroactivity to reopen old cases; the Department explicitly states it will not enforce the final regulations retroactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and coordination with other federal obligations (e.g., Clery Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations should align Title IX obligations with related federal law (such as the Clery Act) to simplify compliance and reduce conflicting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters supported alignment between the proposed rules and the Clery Act so institutions could comply with multiple obligations more easily and consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles: take survivors seriously while ensuring fairness for accused
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-negotiable principles include taking every survivor seriously and ensuring every person accused knows guilt is not predetermined; balancing these principles should guide rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary emphasized both the importance of taking survivors seriously and protecting due process rights of the accused; the final regulations are presented as seeking a 'better way forward' that works for all students.
